h: Earthquakes, Glens and a Grand Day in Strathearn
p: Comrie has a cracking claim to fame that most visitors never hear about: it's known as the shaky toun because it sits on the Highland Boundary Fault and has a long history of small earth tremors. On the edge of the village you'll find the Earthquake House, a tiny Victorian building that holds a replica of an early seismometer used to record the tremors. You peer in through the window rather than going inside, which makes it a quick, quirky stop on the way to or from the park, and kids love the idea that the ground here occasionally wobbles.

At the park itself, think about the order you do things. Younger kids often have more patience for the animals early on and are ready to let rip in the play areas later, so leaving the adventure side until after lunch can save a meltdown. Take a picnic if the weather is kind, as the hillside setting is a lovely spot to sit, and keep a dry layer in the bag because Perthshire can turn from sunshine to drizzle and back again in an afternoon.

Crieff is the bigger hub of the area and has a proper spa-town feel, with handsome Victorian buildings climbing the hillside. It's also home to the Glenturret distillery, a smart pick for grown-ups after a tour. Drummond Castle Gardens, a few miles south near Muthill, are among the most striking formal gardens in Scotland and famously turned up on screen in Outlander. Head west instead and the road follows the River Earn to St Fillans and Loch Earn, which is about as pretty as a short drive gets.
